newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Nov 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Nov 27.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Czech firms doing business in Russia are calling for more support from the Czech government. Czech businesses operating there are worried about the government's plans to eliminate its network of delegates.

- Konsolidacni Banka, the majority shareholder of Zetor Brno with 80 percent of the company's stocks, is proposing to decrease Zetor's basic capital by 3.7 billion crowns in order to eliminate the company's debts which is necessary to strengthen its export ability. The nominal value of one share would decrease from 1,000 crowns to 110 crowns.
- The Czech Association of Travel Agencies, made up of 200 agencies, has decided to lower the number of places offered in tours next year by 30 percent while increasing tour prices by 10 percent.
- The damage caused by the explosion and fire in Ceska Rafinerska's Litvinov refinery will be hundreds of millions of crowns, according to Ceska Pojistovna. The cause of the fire is still not known.

- The average Czech citizen received 636.4 crowns in social support over the first nine months of 1996, according to the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs. Altogether 16.5 billion crowns has been provided for social support in this period.

- Kablo Elektro a.s., a producer of electric cables and conductors, raised their turnover by 15 percent to 832 million crowns in the first three quarters of 1996 as compared to the same period a year ago. Exports increased from 18 percent of production a year ago to 25 percent this year.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - President Vaclav Havel will undergo an operation next week to discover the cause of problems he is having with his lungs. Havel has had pneumonia for the last two weeks and his case has not improved.

- The removal of Aero Vodochody's debts, recently approved by the government and expected to be confirmed in the company's December shareholder's meeting, could face complications from the current minority owners of the company, banks IPB and CSOB who do not like the government's plan.
PRAVO - The general director of Poldi Ocel, Vladimir Stehlik, and his son, Marek Stehlik, were arrested yesterday for abusing information in the privatisation of the Kladno steel company.
- Rozvodne Elektroenergeticke Spolecnosti is interested in taking part in the privatisation of the Czech banks, according to the general manager of Severoceska Energetika, Jiri Stastny.

- Barum Continental sro posted a gross profit of 400 million crowns in the first nine months of 1996, an increase of 40 percent over the previous year, according to Barum's Jaroslav Cechura. Turnover increased by 12 percent to 5.96 billion crowns.
- A leading international manufacturer and supplier of computer peripherals, Taiwan's Primax, will begin offering its products in the Czech Republic starting December 1.
